# Quota producer contract (PRM-02)

Worker-pool owns `quota_reserve.snapshot()` / `ReserveFloor` and
`cli_fleet._json_payload()` / `FleetQuotaPayload`. The measurement owner remains
`codex_quota_snapshots.QuotaMeasurement`, adopted from QUOTAEMIT-01 (PR 8691).
The field meanings are in [the data-model domain](../../../docs/data-model/02-worker-pool-and-dispatch.md#fleet-quota-reserve-readings-quotaemit-01).
This record follows [the producer-owned convention](../../../docs/contracts/producer-owned-contracts.md).

`reserveFloors` keys name quota provider/account pairs: `openai-oauth`,
`openai-oauth-corp`, `anthropic-oauth`, `anthropic-oauth-corp`. Corporate windows
are independent. `measurement` selects the most constrained unreset window;
`weeklyMeasurement` selects only 10080-minute OpenAI or `seven_day` Anthropic
windows. Both report percentages, ISO observation/reset timestamps and original
window diagnostics. A fresh five-hour window never proves weekly headroom.

A measured weekly object has `status=confidence=measured` and a null reason.
Retained old evidence is an object with `status=confidence=stale` and reason
`stale`. A null weekly object requires `no-weekly-window` (absent, expired or
short-only evidence) or `measurement-unavailable` (failed loading). Expired
windows deliberately share `no-weekly-window` with absent windows: it means
there is no usable weekly window, not that the producer never observed one.
Inspect the raw account probe when triaging missing versus expired evidence. Disabled
floor thresholds still emit available evidence. Missing/invalid keys are
contract defects, distinct from documented null-plus-reason unavailability.

The fleet envelope includes the floors and provider statuses, the broker's
`brokerAuth` (unaltered while fresh), probe heartbeat and last probe time, suspended requests,
dismissed count, exhaustion events, provider-reported holds, and estimated
remaining capacity. `unavailableSections` is optional; adjunct failures retain
the owner's existing empty/null/availability shape. Raw floors omit held counts;
fleet adds integer-or-null `heldCount` and `pauseHeldCount`. It is transient JSON,
not a new store. QUOTAINPUTSTALE-01 preserves the last broker observation when
published inputs are late, with additive `observedAt`, `ageSeconds`, `retained: true`
and `stale: true` fields on retained bodies. `provider_states.<provider>.ready`
and `can_serve` retain their observed values. At 900 seconds from the original
observation, readiness is omitted and `unavailableSections.brokerAuth` reports
staleness. Failed republication never refreshes that observation clock. The
[broker readiness fixture](../test/fixtures/quota-broker-readiness.json) and focused
fleet-status tests cover the review service's expected paths without importing
its repository. JSON status remains exit 0 on successful serialization, with
existing failure exits and stderr behavior unchanged.

## Readers and compatibility

`quota_reserve.weekly_evidence` is the shared Python weekly reader.
`fallback_block` retains its tuple shim; `fallback_evidence` adds producer and
field diagnostics in both dispatch and admission candidate records. Reserve
admission audits identify the paused/active/nearCap field. No threshold, fallback edge,
account preference or allow/hold condition changes. In particular, a measured
status with a malformed percentage gets a diagnostic without a new admission
condition. Unknown/stale weekly evidence retains the existing Claude account
switch hold; Codex retains its existing unknown-evidence policy.

Fleet and harness readiness readers share
`agent_os_core.broker_evidence.provider_evidence`; the broker owns its wire types
and [capture record](../../../platform/oauth-broker/tests/fixtures/contracts/README.md).
Readiness, cached-token servability and refresh-age inspection have distinct
owner policies. Their sibling implementations were inspected and retain those
policies. The existing quota-to-broker name resolver maps OpenAI to `codex`,
Anthropic to `claude-code`, Google to `gemini`, and corporate accounts to the
corresponding `-corp` name. Broker-wire readers do not invent provider aliases.

## Captures and exact recapture

Producer repository: `agent-os`. Emitting logic revision:
`2f686a90a102cf52e631dbf597d3e85826dc7b5d`; quota repair revision:
`36da525326825a94db3c02433f9b0b4fc496da8c`. PRM-02 adds return annotations,
readers and capture tests; it does not change the serialized producer semantics.
The capture harness/input definitions are in this PR's
[`test_quota_reserve_weekly.py`](../lib/python/tests/test_quota_reserve_weekly.py).

Examples live in [`fixtures/quota_reserve`](../lib/python/tests/fixtures/quota_reserve):

- `repaired-{measured,disabled,absent,five-hour-only,expired,stale,unavailable}.json`:
  actual `snapshot()` over four independent account inputs. Fixed observation
  clock is 2026-10-20T03:00:00Z; short windows use 95% and weekly windows use
  25%/40% for primary/corporate. Anthropic input files use the real usage parser;
  OpenAI reader inputs are account-stamped rows, with no borrowed burn history.
  These captures have no normalization.
- `fleet-{ready,unavailable,degraded,disabled}.json`: actual `cmd_status` JSON
  stdout (exit 0, empty stderr), including `_status_payload`, worker outcomes
  and `_json_payload`, over disposable quota files, an empty follow-up log and
  a migrated empty SQLite ledger. Real file readers, accounting queries and serializers execute.
  External broker observations reuse the broker captures; review-store transport
  returns no review rows. Only temporary-root path prefixes become `<scratch>`.
- `reserveFloors-capture-2026-10-20.json` remains negative pre-repair reproduction
  evidence; its source revision is unknown. Its unexplained null OpenAI weekly
  fields and empty floors both fail the plan's unchanged activation predicate.

From the repository root, after capturing the broker examples first:

```bash
export NETGUARD_ROOT="${NETGUARD_ROOT:?set to your provisioned netguard root}"
test -d "$NETGUARD_ROOT/bin" && test -d "$NETGUARD_ROOT/site"
NETGUARD_LOG=/tmp/prm02-quota-recapture.log \
PATH="$NETGUARD_ROOT/bin:$PATH" PYTHONPATH="$NETGUARD_ROOT/site" \
AGENT_OS_SESSION_LEDGER_VDB=false PRM_RECAPTURE=1 \
"${PYTHON:-python3}" -c 'import subprocess,sys; raise SystemExit(subprocess.run([sys.executable,"-m","pytest","modules/worker-pool/lib/python/tests/test_quota_reserve_weekly.py","-k","producer_capture_parity","-q","--disable-warnings"],timeout=180).returncode)'
```

`NETGUARD_ROOT/bin` must contain the command wrappers and `site` the
socket-free Python guard, as described in the broker capture record. Set
`PYTHON` to an interpreter with the worker-pool test dependencies installed.
`PRM_RECAPTURE=1` writes only the selected actual outputs and marks the capture
tests skipped; rerun without it to verify parity. Snapshot equality covers
`reserveFloors` and `brokerAuth`; unrelated fleet envelope fields use shape checks.
Negative tests explicitly mutate missing/null/wrong-type fields, percentage types and unknown
statuses. Consumer tests load these same examples. Activation-predicate tests
invoke jq on the existing plan assertion; runtime never reads projects.

## Deployment

No configuration, schema migration or privileged activation is required.
CLI readers load the code on their next invocation. Long-running dispatch
readers receive diagnostics on their normal registered reload; this worker
performs no restart. Same-user read-only verification is
`hq fleet quota status --json`: inspect each floor's weekly object/reason and
compare weekly consumption with that account's text status. This does not
probe credentials or authorize launching the parked pack. Lifecycle states,
transitions, smoke promises and enforcement policy are unchanged.
